general_background.title: Selenium delivery from TOP–Se
general_background.summary: Trioctylphosphine selenide carries selenium in a soluble feed, rather than as separate solid selenium. The conversion of that feed can affect how much selenium is available while nuclei form and grow.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Synthesis and characterization of nearly monodisperse CdE (E = sulfur, selenium, tellurium) semiconductor nanocrystallites

general_background.title: A thiol can both supply sulfur and bind the surface
general_background.summary: In metal-sulfide routes that use an alkanethiol as the sulfur feed, metal–thiolate chemistry can supply sulfur to the growing lattice. Thiol or thiolate species can also bind at the particle surface, so sulfur delivery and surface capping may be linked.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Selective Nanocrystal Synthesis and Calculated Electronic Structure of All Four Phases of Copper–Antimony–Sulfide

general_background.title: A reactive phosphide feed changes growth timing
general_background.summary: Tris(trimethylsilyl)phosphine reacts with indium carboxylate in common colloidal indium phosphide routes. Rapid precursor conversion does not necessarily make all particles form at once, because molecular clusters can participate before continued crystal growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Two-Step Nucleation and Growth of InP Quantum Dots via Magic-Sized Cluster Intermediates

general_background.title: Stable cluster intermediates can delay particle growth
general_background.summary: In some indium phosphide routes, unusually stable molecular clusters accumulate instead of turning immediately into a smoothly growing distribution. Their appearance breaks the simple link between mixing the precursor and forming the final nanocrystals.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
